# AKS Security Advisories -- machine-readable feed guide

> GENERATED with this feed build (2026-08-07T20:17:45Z). Every byte size, release label and
> count below is a fact about THIS build, walked from manifest.json and the
> canonical vocabulary -- not a hand-written claim. Re-read manifest.json /
> glossary.json for the authoritative live inventory.

Community, open-source security-advisory data for Azure Kubernetes Service
(AKS) node images. It tracks per-CVE fix status for the Azure Linux and
Ubuntu base packages baked into the AKS VHD. It is NOT an official
Microsoft/Azure product and NOT an authoritative source of truth for AKS
security posture.

Base URL: https://chrischangcode.github.io/aks-security-advisory/
Data root: https://chrischangcode.github.io/aks-security-advisory/data/

## Scope boundaries

- Covers: AKS node-image (VHD) base OS packages (Azure Linux + Ubuntu).
- Does NOT cover: the container/OCI images AKS ships (a separate product,
  tracked in issue #40) -- do not answer container-image questions from
  this feed.
- Only executables under /bin and /sbin are indexed by the path maps; a
  path outside those prefixes is OUT OF SCOPE, not 'clean' (see F6 below).
- Absence of data for a (CVE, lineage) pair means NOT ASSESSED, not NOT
  AFFECTED. Never infer safety from a miss.

Read manifest.json FIRST to plan fetches and avoid the large index.json.
Endpoints marked 'optional' may be absent on an older feed artifact; treat
a 404 on them as 'this feed predates the endpoint', not an error.
Every path above is data-root-relative, e.g. https://chrischangcode.github.io/aks-security-advisory/data/index.json

## Status vocabulary (from glossary.json; counts measured in this build)

- fixed (Fixed) -- count 7123
    A scanned AKS VHD build ships a package version at or above the distro's fixed version. The 'first fixed build' field names the earliest build that carries the fix.
- fix_available_upstream (Fix available upstream) -- count 13
    The distro (Azure Linux / Ubuntu) has published a fixed package, but none of the scanned VHD builds ship it yet. The fix exists upstream and is expected in a future node image.
- affected (Affected) -- count 5120
    Vulnerable, with no fix AKS can ship yet. Comes from a vendor VEX / Ubuntu CVE Tracker assertion (a fixless CVE cannot be enumerated from OVAL alone), or from the binary scan overlay when a CVE survives to the newest scanned build. A scanned binary stays affected even if the scanner reports a fixed version, because that fix is in the bundled module and not in any artifact AKS ships — see evidence.module_fixed_version. The generated glossary records how large a share of the feed it is.
- not_affected (Not affected) -- count 5016
    Excluded by a vendor verdict — an Azure Linux CSAF/VEX justification or an Ubuntu CVE Tracker 'not-affected' (e.g. the vulnerable code path is not present/reachable). The justification is shown on the advisory.
- under_investigation (Under investigation) -- count 326
    Triage is not complete — either no distro OVAL/VEX verdict exists yet, or the Ubuntu CVE Tracker marks the package 'needs-triage'.
- will_not_fix (Will not fix) -- count 790
    The vendor will not ship a fix (Ubuntu CVE Tracker 'ignored' — e.g. the release is past standard support, or the fix is deemed too intrusive). The reason is shown on the advisory.

Do NOT assume any status is rare; consult glossary.json status.counts /
shares. IMPORTANT: those are the per-advisory HEADLINE distribution (one
most-actionable status per advisory), NOT per-package-row prevalence -- do
not read status.shares.affected as 'the share of my packages that are
affected' (that is the F7 misread). glossary.json status.counts_basis states
this inline.

## Coverage vocabulary (extended binaries; from glossary.json)

- covered_by_package (Covered by package)
    This extended binary is the same artifact as an installed distro package that the distro advisory feed actually tracks, so its CVE status IS assessed — see the linked package's advisories.
- covered_by_scan (Covered by scan)
    Assessed by a binary (Trivy) scan of the extended binary itself, because the distro advisory feeds don't track it. Carries scan evidence rather than a distro package row. Only downloadable binary archives are scanned — tarballs and .deb/.rpm packages — while components shipped as container/OCI images are classified 'container_image' and not scanned.
- scan_pending (Scan pending)
    Installed as a distro package (typically a Microsoft-repackaged one from packages.microsoft.com — e.g. moby-containerd, moby-runc, aznfs) that the base distro's advisory feed does NOT track. Its status is honestly unknown here; a binary scan is planned. Not treated as covered.
- aks_built (AKS-built / upstream)
    Built by AKS or downloaded from upstream as a downloadable archive/package (oras, Azure CNI, cni-plugins, acr-mirror). No distro package exists for it in the base feed, so distro OVAL/CVE feeds do not track it; it is scanned by the binary overlay where an archive is available.
- container_image (Container image)
    Built/distributed by AKS as an OCI container image rather than a downloadable archive (kubelet/kubectl via the kubernetes-node image, azure-acr-credential-provider). The binary scan overlay assesses downloadable archives, not images, so these are not scanned here and are tracked by their own upstream.
- not_baked (Not baked in)
    A distro package installed only conditionally (e.g. GPU drivers / DCGM at node provisioning) and absent from the mainstream baked image — nothing to assess for this lineage.
- not_assessed (Not assessed)
    Not tracked by the distro advisory feeds (e.g. cached container images).

## Hard rules for agents (do not violate)

F4/F5 -- INSTALL PATHS ARE PER-FAMILY. Each VHD family (Ubuntu vs Azure
Linux, and each generation/SKU lineage) has DIFFERENT binary install paths.
A path that owns package X on one family may not exist, or may map
elsewhere, on another. Resolve a path WITHIN a lineage (pick the pathmap for
that lineage), NEVER against a global/merged map. Both usr-merge spellings
(/bin/x and /usr/bin/x) are materialized as real keys in by_path; use
by_base for a basename fallback.

F6 -- A MISS IS 'UNKNOWN', NOT 'NOT VULNERABLE'. If a path lookup, a
by-package lookup, or a (CVE, lineage) pair finds nothing, that is UNKNOWN /
not-assessed, never 'safe'. The pathmap carries coverage_note and
indexed_prefixes saying so; only /bin and /sbin executables are indexed, so
a .so / JAR / Go binary path is out of scope, not clean. Report unknown.

F7 -- headline_status IS NOT PER-SKU. advisory.headline_status is the
MOST-ACTIONABLE status across ALL lineages (ranked). Reading it as the
status of one specific SKU is wrong. For a SKU-level answer read the
packages[] row whose releases[] CONTAINS your lineage label in
advisories/<ID>.json -- one row covers every lineage sharing that
assessment, so test membership, not equality.
glossary.json status.counts is likewise headline-derived -- its
status.counts_basis field says so; do not contradict it.

## Worked recipe: a (binary path, CVE) spreadsheet row

Goal: given a scanner row (absolute binary path, CVE) and the node's VHD
lineage, report the AKS fix status -- without guessing.

1. GET manifest.json -- inventory endpoints + sizes; plan fetches.
2. Pick the pathmap for the row's lineage: GET pathmap/index.json, map the
   lineage label to its key, then GET pathmap/<key>.json. Look up the exact
   path in by_path (try both usr-merge spellings; fall back to by_base on the
   basename). This yields the owning package(s) FOR THAT FAMILY (F4/F5). No
   owner -> UNKNOWN, not clean (F6).
3. GET by-package/index.json, resolve the package name to its file (or its
   alias); do NOT construct the filename. Then GET by-package/<file>.json and
   find your CVE id in advisories[].
   If MORE THAN ONE row matches your lineage (rare, but possible), take the
   MOST ACTIONABLE status -- the same ranking headline_status uses -- rather
   than the first match.

4. GET advisories/<CVE>.json and read the packages[] row whose releases[]
   CONTAINS your lineage label -- THAT row's status is the SKU-level answer
   (NOT headline_status, F7). Rows identical apart from the lineage are
   merged, so match by membership. No row listing your lineage -> NOT
   ASSESSED (F6).

Worked example resolved from THIS build (replay it verbatim -- every
identifier is verified to resolve):

  input path : /usr/bin/openssl
  input CVE  : CVE-2026-42769
  lineage    : AKSAzureLinuxV3/gen2  (pathmap key: azurelinux-3.0)
  step 2     : pathmap/azurelinux-3.0.json by_path['/usr/bin/openssl'] -> owns 'openssl'
  step 3     : by-package/index.json -> 'openssl' resolves to by-package/openssl.json
  step 3     : by-package/openssl.json lists CVE-2026-42769 in advisories[]
  step 4     : advisories/CVE-2026-42769.json packages[] -> read the row whose
               releases[] contains your lineage, for the SKU-level status

Machine-readable form of the worked example:
{"cve": "CVE-2026-42769", "lineage": "AKSAzureLinuxV3/gen2", "package": "openssl", "package_file": "openssl.json", "path": "/usr/bin/openssl", "pathmap_key": "azurelinux-3.0"}

## Other descriptors

- schema.json    -- JSON Schema for these documents (data-root).
- dataset.jsonld -- schema.org Dataset (distribution[] mirrors the data
                    endpoints above).
- sitemap.xml    -- every endpoint + per-advisory URL.
- A stable, human-readable data contract is published as DATA-CONTRACT.md at
  the site root.

These four descriptor files are themselves inventoried in manifest.json (the
endpoint inventory is exhaustive), so enumerating manifest.json reveals the
whole discovery layer, not just the data endpoints.
